key_insight: SAMA factorizes instruction-guided video editing into two complementary components—Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment—so the model can apply precise semantic edits while faithfully preserving original motion, without heavy reliance on external priors.
problem_solved: Balances accurate, instruction-driven semantic changes with temporal/motion fidelity in video editing, addressing robustness and generalization limits caused by dependence on external priors (e.g., VLM features or structural conditions).
method: Semantic Anchoring: isolate and apply instruction-specified semantic modifications to target objects/regions while keeping anchored appearance cues to avoid drift.
Motion Alignment: explicitly model and preserve temporal motion patterns (e.g., flow or temporal features) to maintain realistic, coherent movement across frames.
Internal factorization strategy: combine the two modules in a unified pipeline that reduces reliance on external priors, improving robustness and generalization to diverse videos and instructions.
impact: Enables practitioners to produce more faithful, instruction-guided video edits that retain original motion and temporal coherence, reducing engineering effort for external conditioning and improving performance on varied real-world inputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two parallel branches: Semantic Anchoring (semantic map / text → edit) and Motion Alignment (flow / temporal stream → preserve motion), merging into edited video output.

paper_title: SAMA: Factorized Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
paper_authors: Xinyao Zhang, Wenkai Dong, Yuxin Song, Bo Fang, Qi Zhang
